newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Power outage interrupts soccer in Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: Power outage interrupts soccer in Guatemala.

text.p: A power outage on Wednesday night plunged most of Guatemala's capital into darkness for almost two hours and temporarily interrupted a Central American soccer tournament.
The tournament was held at the stadium where 78 fans were killed last October when crowding triggered a human avalanche in the worst soccer tragedy in the history of World Cup qualifying.
No crowd control problems were reported during Wednesday night's two-hour outage.
"The outage is due to a failure in the control room in southern Guatemala City," a spokesman for the National Electrification Institute told Reuters.
The power went out at approximately 6:30 p.m. (2330 GMT) and was restored to most of the capital two hours later.

The lights came and went twice in a central part of Guatemala City, interrupting a match between the national teams of Costa Rica and Honduras, playing in the IV Cup of Nations at Mateo Flores stadium.
The teams left the field twice, only to return to the pitch and resume play where they left off. Costa Rica won 4-0.
Costa Rica was to play Guatemala last October, but the match was canceled when the tragedy occurred about half an hour before kickoff.
